title: shanghai exchange adjust trading limits some oil futures contracts 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - The Shanghai Futures Exchange will adjust ​trading limits for some oil futures contracts ‌from the night trading session on September 14, it said on Friday.
The announcement came as oil ​prices were on track for a ​weekly gain of more than 7% as ⁠attacks along key Middle East shipping ​routes stoked prolonged supply disruption fears.
The Shanghai International ​Energy Exchange, a subsidiary of the Shanghai Futures Exchange, said in statements that it would limit ​the maximum intraday opening positions for crude ​oil and low-sulfur fuel oil futures contracts with delivery ‌in ⁠October and November to 800 lots and 3,000 lots, respectively.
It will also adjust the price limit range for the crude ​oil and low-sulfur ​fuel ⁠oil futures contracts with delivery in October and November to 16%, ​trading margins for hedging positions to ​17%.
The ⁠statements did not disclose the previous limits, and the exchange could not immediately be ⁠reached ​for comment outside of ​normal business hours.
